q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The computer-based Hindi learning package 'LILA', developed for the Department of Official Language, stands for Learning Indian Languages through Artificial Intelligence.
2. The first Hindi newspaper 'Udant Martand' was edited by Bharatendu Harishchandra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Fort William College at Calcutta, associated with the development of Hindi prose, was established in the year 1800 by Lord Wellesley.
2. 'Prem Sagar', an early prose work in Khari Boli Hindi produced at the Fort William College, was written by Lallu Lal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The three-language formula for school education was first recommended by the Education Commission (Kothari Commission), 1964-66.
2. Under the National Education Policy, 2020, wherever possible, the medium of instruction should be the mother tongue/local language until at least Class V.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, containing the targets to be achieved by Central Government offices, is issued by the Department of Official Language every year.
2. The different percentage targets for Hindi correspondence prescribed for Regions 'A', 'B' and 'C' are graded according to the linguistic environment of the region, the highest being for Region 'A' and the lowest for Region 'C'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Policy of the Union is implemented in Central Government offices mainly through persuasion, encouragement and incentives, and not through compulsion.
2. The classification of States into Region 'A', Region 'B' and Region 'C' under the Official Language Rules is based mainly on the extent to which Hindi is the official language of the State and is widely spoken and understood there.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Besides official members, the Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of a Union Ministry includes Members of Parliament and non-official members nominated from among Hindi scholars and experts.
2. In a Railway Division, the day-to-day work relating to the implementation of the Official Language Policy is looked after by the Rajbhasha Adhikari (Official Language Officer).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The "Brihad Prashasan Shabdavali" (Comprehensive Glossary of Administrative Terms), the standard reference for Hindi equivalents of administrative terms, is published by the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology.
2. The standard form of the Devanagari script and of Hindi spelling (Manak Vartani), adopted for official use, was prepared by the Central Hindi Directorate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Hindi translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts is prepared by the Official Language Wing (Rajbhasha Khand) of the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice.
2. The headquarters of the Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) is located at New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities is located at Prayagraj (Allahabad).
2. The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions under the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing exactly 70 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:

In a Central Government office, exactly 80 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, as notification requires more than 90 per cent of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.C: The office cannot be notified, as notification depends on the total number of staff and not on any proportion
options.D: The office can be notified only during Hindi Pakhwada

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 30 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He fails, the prescribed speed being 40 words per minute
options.B: He fails, the prescribed speed being 35 words per minute
options.C: His result is withheld, speed alone being insufficient for passing
options.D: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 30 words per minute

q: A member of the Legislature of a State is unable to express himself adequately in the official language of the State, in Hindi or in English, and wishes to address the House in his mother tongue. Under Article 210 of the Constitution, he may do so with the permission of:

options.B: The presiding officer of the House
options.C: The Chief Minister of the State

q: An employee records his noting on a file in Hindi. His superior officer directs him to also furnish an English translation of the noting. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The employee must furnish the translation immediately on demand
options.B: The translation has to be prepared by the Hindi Translator at the employee's cost
options.C: The employee cannot be required to furnish a translation of his noting in the other language
options.D: Only a gazetted officer is exempt from furnishing such a translation

q: A Central Government office issues a notice inviting applications from the public in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, such a notice is required to be issued in:

options.B: Hindi only, as issued by the office
options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

q: A Central Government office prints the headings of its registers in English only. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the headings of registers used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in:

options.A: English only, as registers are internal records

q: After the expiration of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, an objection is raised that English can no longer be used for the transaction of business in Parliament. Under Article 120(2) of the Constitution, the use of English for that purpose was to discontinue after fifteen years, unless:

options.A: The President by order otherwise provides
options.C: The Official Language Commission recommends otherwise

q: A Central Government office procures a software package which has the facility of working in English only. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, software packages procured for use in Central Government offices are required to have:

options.A: The facility of working in Hindi only, with no provision for English
options.B: The facility of working only in the regional language of the State of posting
options.C: The facility of working in Hindi as well, i.e., bilingual (Hindi-English) capability
options.D: No language facility, Hindi work being done only on typewriters

q: A State Government office located in Region 'A' ordinarily corresponds with Central Government offices in English, on the ground that English is understood in all offices. The correct position is that such an office ordinarily corresponds with Central Government offices in:

options.B: The regional language, through the Governor's Secretariat
options.C: Both Hindi and English, every letter being issued in two copies
options.D: English only, as a matter of rule

q: Fifteen years have expired from the commencement of the Constitution, and a question arises whether English may continue to be used for transacting business in the Legislature of a State. Under Article 210(2) of the Constitution, the use of English for that purpose ceases on the expiration of fifteen years, unless:

options.A: The President by order otherwise provides
options.B: The Governor of the State directs otherwise
options.D: The Legislature of the State by law otherwise provides

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 29 of the Constitution guarantees to any section of the citizens having a distinct language, script or culture of its own, the right to conserve the same.
2. The authoritative text of the Constitution of India in the Hindi language is published under the authority of the President in accordance with Article 394A.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The expression used in Part XVII of the Constitution for the status of Hindi in the Union is "Official Language of the Union".
2. The Constitution does not declare any language as the national language of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350A of the Constitution, it shall be the endeavour of every State and every local authority within the State to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
2. Under Article 350A of the Constitution, the President may issue such directions to any State as he considers necessary or proper for securing the provision of such facilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the President.
2. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, it shall be the duty of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities to investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the authoritative texts of all Bills introduced in Parliament or in a State Legislature, and of all Acts passed by them, shall be in English.
2. Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the authoritative texts of all orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws issued under the Constitution or under any law made by Parliament or the Legislature of a State shall be in English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under the proviso to Article 210(2) of the Constitution, in relation to the Legislatures of the States of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, the period of fifteen years for the continued use of English in the State Legislature was substituted by a period of twenty-five years.
2. Under Article 120(2) of the Constitution, the use of the English language for the transaction of business in Parliament was to discontinue after fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, unless Parliament by law otherwise provides.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Hindi Teaching Scheme for imparting in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees was introduced in the year 1955.
2. The first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission) was appointed by the President on 7th June, 1955.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The award of the Department of Official Language for excellence in the implementation of the Official Language Policy, now known as the Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar, was earlier known as the Indira Gandhi Rajbhasha Puraskar.
2. The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar and the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language are presented every year on the occasion of Hindi Diwas (14th September).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. LILA, the computer-based Hindi learning package developed for the Department of Official Language, stands for Learning Indian Languages through Artificial Intelligence.
2. For doing Hindi work on computers in Central Government offices, the font/encoding that should be used, so that the document can be read and exchanged on any computer system, is a Unicode-compliant font (such as Mangal).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The official languages of the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands are Hindi and English.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands is placed in Region 'A'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the Union Territory of Chandigarh is English.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the Union Territory of Chandigarh is placed in Region 'B'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the National Capital Territory of Delhi is Hindi.
2. The second official languages of the National Capital Territory of Delhi are Punjabi and Urdu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Tripura is Bengali.
2. Kokborok is one of the official languages of the State of Tripura.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of Telangana.
2. Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of West Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. English is one of the official languages of the State of Sikkim.
2. Hindi is not one of the official languages of the State of Sikkim.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Act of Goa (the Goa, Daman and Diu Official Language Act), under which Konkani was declared the official language of the State, was enacted in the year 1987.
2. The Konkani language is written in as many as five scripts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Kashmiri language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, is officially written in the Perso-Arabic script.
2. The Kashmiri language belongs to the Dardic group of the Indo-Aryan family of languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The script invented for writing the Santhali language, known as Ol Chiki, was invented in the year 1925 by Pandit Raghunath Murmu.
2. The Gurmukhi script, in which the Punjabi language is written, was standardised by Guru Angad Dev.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. At present, the Manipuri language is written for official purposes mainly in the Bengali script.
2. The traditional script of the Manipuri language is the Meitei Mayek script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The word 'Hindi' is derived from the Persian word 'Hind', which itself has its origin in the Sanskrit word 'Sindhu'.
2. The colloquial spoken language formed by the blend of Hindi and Persian is commonly known as Hindustani.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The 'Ramcharitmanas' of Goswami Tulsidas is written in Awadhi.
2. 'Dakkhini', an early literary form of the Hindi-Urdu speech, developed mainly in the region of Punjab.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Haryana is Hindi.
2. The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Maharashtra is Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011:
1. The number of persons who returned Hindi as their mother tongue was approximately 43 crore.
2. In terms of the total number of speakers in the world, Hindi ranks third, after English and Mandarin Chinese.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Kumaoni and Garhwali dialects belong to the Western Hindi group of dialects.
2. The Marwari dialect is a dialect of Rajasthani.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Awadhi dialect belongs to the Eastern Hindi group of Hindi dialects.
2. The Braj Bhasha dialect belongs to the Eastern Hindi group of Hindi dialects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing exactly 60 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing exactly 55 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing exactly 90 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks
options.B: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi stenography examination
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing exactly 88 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 90 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Pragya examination
options.C: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the stenography examination being 88 per cent or more marks
options.D: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of exactly 80 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He fails, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.B: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 80 words per minute
options.C: He fails, the prescribed speed being 90 words per minute
options.D: His result is withheld, speed alone being insufficient for passing

q: An employee who has attained the age of exactly 45 years does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He must undergo the training, as in-service Hindi training is compulsory for every employee irrespective of age
options.B: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.C: He must undergo the training on payment of the prescribed fee
options.D: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of exactly 10,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.B: He is not eligible, the prescribed minimum being 50,000 words in a year
options.C: He is eligible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination with 70 per cent or more marks
options.D: He is eligible only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976

q: A town has exactly ten Central Government offices. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town:

options.A: No committee can be constituted, as a Town Official Language Implementation Committee requires at least fifty Central Government offices
options.B: A committee can be constituted only by the District Magistrate of the town
options.C: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee (Nagar Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) can be constituted, such a committee being constituted in a town or city which has ten or more Central Government offices
options.D: A committee can be constituted only during Hindi Pakhwada

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the thirteenth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 24 months
options.B: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 12 months only
options.C: The claim is in order, personal pay being admissible for the entire remaining service
options.D: The claim is in order only if the employee passes the examination again

q: A Central Government office spends exactly one-half of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books. Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, the office:

options.A: Has not complied with the target, at least 75 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.B: Has not complied with the target, the entire amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.C: Has not complied with the target, at least 55 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.D: Has complied with the target, at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for office libraries being required to be spent on Hindi books

q: Which of the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011, is FALSE?

options.A: Hindi is the mother tongue of about 43.6 per cent of the population of India
options.B: Among the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, Sanskrit has the largest number of speakers
options.C: The number of mother tongues returned in the raw returns of the Census was 19,569
options.D: The number of languages each spoken by 10,000 or more persons is 121

q: Which of the following statements about the official languages of the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh is FALSE?

options.A: Under the Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020, the number of languages declared as the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is five
options.B: Kashmiri is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under that Act
options.C: Hindi is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under that Act
options.D: Punjabi is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under that Act

q: Which of the following pairs of an English administrative term and its standard Hindi equivalent is NOT correctly matched?
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 3(2) from Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Both the provisions deal only with the documents to be issued in both Hindi and English
options.B: Section 3(2) deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 3(3) deals with the rule-making power of the Central Government
options.C: Section 3(2) provides for the language to be used for communication between the Union and a State, while Section 3(3) provides that specified documents, such as resolutions, general orders, notifications, contracts and tender forms, shall be issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: Section 3(2) requires specified documents to be issued in both Hindi and English, while Section 3(3) deals with communication between the Union and a State

q: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the following events relating to the Official Language?

options.A: Official Language Rules — Official Languages Act — Official Language Resolution — Department of Official Language
options.B: Official Languages Act — Official Language Resolution — Department of Official Language — Official Language Rules
options.C: Official Language Resolution — Official Languages Act — Official Language Rules — Department of Official Language
options.D: Department of Official Language — Official Languages Act — Official Language Resolution — Official Language Rules

q: A Central Government office prepares its bye-laws and proposes to issue them in English only. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the bye-laws are required to be issued in:

options.B: English only, as proposed by the office
options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

q: A newly opened branch of a Central Government office gets its rubber stamps prepared in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. Under the Rajbhasha implementation instructions, the rubber stamps used in the office should be prepared:

options.A: In Hindi only, as prepared by the office
options.D: In bilingual form, i.e., in Hindi and English

q: A Hindi-speaking citizen telephones a Central Government office and begins the conversation in Hindi. The official attending the call replies to him in English throughout, on the ground that telephone replies are official communications. The correct position is that the official should, as far as possible, reply to him:

options.B: In English only, as was done
options.C: Only after transferring the call to the Hindi Cell
options.D: In the regional language of the office

q: A Central Government office prints its manuals and codes in English only, on the ground that they are technical publications meant for officers. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature of Central Government offices are required to be printed and published in:

options.A: English only, as proposed by the office
options.C: Diglot form, i.e., in Hindi and English

q: At a railway station, the name boards are displayed in the order: Hindi, English, Regional language. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that name boards, designation boards and sign boards at railway stations and offices are required to be displayed in three languages, in the order:

options.A: Hindi, English, Regional language, as displayed at the station

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 349 of the Constitution, during the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, no Bill or amendment relating to the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts could be introduced in either House of Parliament without the previous sanction of the President.
2. The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) was set up in the year 1967.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 347 of the Constitution, where the President directs that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall be officially recognised, such recognition may be for the whole or any part of the State and for such purposes as he may specify.
2. On the occasion of Hindi Diwas, the employees of Central Government offices take the Rajbhasha pledge (Rajbhasha Pratigya), to use Hindi to the maximum possible extent in their official work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Chapter I of Part XVII of the Constitution (Articles 343 and 344) is titled "Language of the Union".
2. Chapter IV of Part XVII of the Constitution comprises Articles 348 and 349.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Languages Act, 1963 is Act No. 19 of 1963.
2. The Official Language Resolution, embodying the policy for the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union, was adopted by Parliament in the year 1968.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under clause (2) of Article 343 of the Constitution, during the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, the President could, by order, authorise the use of the Devanagari form of numerals in addition to the international form of Indian numerals.
2. Under Section 3(1) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, notwithstanding the expiration of the period of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, English may continue to be used, in addition to Hindi, for all the official purposes of the Union and for the transaction of business in Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a translation in Hindi of any Central Act or Ordinance, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.
2. Under Article 348(3) of the Constitution, where a State Legislature has prescribed a language other than English for use in Bills introduced in, or Acts passed by, that Legislature, a translation of the same in English, published under the authority of the Governor in the Official Gazette of the State, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in the English language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the use of Hindi, or the official language of a State, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court may be authorised by the Governor of the State, with the previous consent of the President.
2. Under Article 348(2) of the Constitution, the use of Hindi or any other language used for official purposes of a State, in the proceedings of a High Court having its principal seat in that State, may be authorised by the Governor of the State, with the previous consent of the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The first Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee on Official Language was Om Mehta.
2. The Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The first Chairman of the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti was Lalit Narayan Mishra.
2. The Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy in Region 'C'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Implementation Committee of the headquarters office of a Zonal Railway is chaired by the General Manager.
2. At the headquarters of a Zonal Railway, the work relating to implementation of the Official Language Policy is looked after by the Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari (Chief Official Language Officer).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) was set up in the year 1971.
2. The Central Translation Bureau functions as a subordinate office of the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology (CSTT) was set up in the year 1961.
2. The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, meant for employees who cannot attend regular training classes, are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Official Language was set up as a separate department in the Ministry of Home Affairs in the year 1975.
2. The Hindi Teaching Scheme (Hindi Shikshan Yojana) for Central Government employees is administered by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Hindi Teaching Scheme for imparting in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees was introduced in the year 1955.
2. The Parangat course, meant for employees who have passed Pragya and require advanced proficiency in Hindi, is conducted through correspondence by the Central Hindi Directorate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the Prabodh course is intended for employees who do not possess any knowledge of Hindi, i.e., beginners.
2. In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the Praveen course is the course to be undergone after passing the Pragya examination.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The training imparted to Central Government employees under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is free of cost during office hours, the training period being treated as on duty.
2. In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is imparted to employees all over the country through a single training centre located at Agra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The websites of Central Government offices are required to be maintained in Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form.
2. The reservation charts (list of passengers) displayed at railway stations are printed in three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The passenger tickets issued by the Indian Railways are printed in Hindi and English.
2. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the letter-heads used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in Hindi and English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Which one of the following statements relating to the institutions for the promotion, teaching and translation of Hindi is FALSE?

options.A: The Central Hindi Directorate was established in the year 1960
options.B: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology functions under the Ministry of Education
options.C: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi), Agra functions under the Ministry of Education
options.D: The Central Translation Bureau functions under the Ministry of Education

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) from the Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of a Union Ministry?

options.A: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti, the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by the Prime Minister, while the Hindi Salahakar Samiti of a Union Ministry is chaired by the Minister in charge of the Ministry
options.B: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti is chaired by the Minister in charge of the Ministry, while the Hindi Salahakar Samiti of a Union Ministry is chaired by the Prime Minister
options.C: Both the committees are chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language
options.D: Both the committees function only at the level of Zonal Railways

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 3(1) from Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Section 3(1) deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 4 provides for the continued use of English
options.B: Section 3(1) provides that, notwithstanding the expiration of the period of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, English may continue to be used, in addition to Hindi, for the official purposes of the Union and for the transaction of business in Parliament, while Section 4 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.C: Both the Sections deal only with the documents to be issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: Both the Sections deal only with the rule-making power of the Central Government

q: A Central Government office enters into an agreement with a supplier and proposes to execute it in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the agreement is required to be executed in:

options.A: Hindi only, as proposed by the office
options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

q: A Central Government office has to send an ordinary communication to an office of a State Government located in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such a communication shall be in:

options.C: The regional language of the State
options.D: Hindi accompanied by its English translation in every case

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 64 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 73 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 94 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi stenography examination
options.C: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 85 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 80 words per minute
options.B: He fails, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.C: He fails, the prescribed speed being 90 words per minute
options.D: His result is withheld, speed alone being insufficient for passing

q: An employee aged 44 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 40 years
options.B: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He must undergo the training on payment of the prescribed fee

q: In a Central Government office, 85 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, as notification requires more than 90 per cent of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, as notification depends on the total number of staff and not on any proportion
options.C: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: The office can be notified only during Hindi Pakhwada

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 12,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible, the prescribed minimum being 50,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination with 70 per cent or more marks
options.C: He is eligible only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976
options.D: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
